- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive after prolonged negative streaks, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is weak (avg sentiment < -0.4); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for lagged sentiment effect.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3-day window), model exhibits overfitting to recent history; smooth forecast by 1–2% to reduce noise sensitivity.
